adversarial_review.check: The hostile lane calls the envelope with alpha=1 and the helper rejects it because the reciprocal exponent is not greater than one.
A reversed toy spectrum changes both the quadratic and alpha=9/10 counting constants.
Multiplying by lambda^alpha instead of dividing by lambda^alpha changes the toy constant and is rejected.
A linear k constant inserted into the retained k^2 envelope gives a negative toy residual and is rejected.
The first positive inverse eigenvalue is strictly below the full inverse-spectrum trace on both selected rows.
Exactly d-1 positive modes above the declared floor are required; a diagonal generator produces no graph edges or positive modes.
The finite sum is checked before the integral tail comparison, so the infinite bound is not treated as a finite equality.
Finite positivity of several C_alpha values does not imply a common exponent or constant, a common core, GNS coercivity, a physical gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite sublinear spectral-counting and zeta-tail checkpoint only. It proves no cutoff-, volume-, source-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform bound, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
decision_reason: Allowing any declared sublinear exponent 0<alpha<1 converts the finite normalized Green-trace target into an explicit mode-counting and zeta-tail condition. Primary, independent, hostile, integrated and Lean checks validate the finite implication, while no data establish that an exponent or counting constant remains bounded under a regulator or thermodynamic limit.
finding: The primary lane passes 508279/508279 assertions over 7 systems, 2688 contexts and 21120 conditional rows; the independent lane passes 508279/508279; the hostile lane passes 8/8; the integrated verifier passes 48/48; and Lean R411 compiles. The retained quadratic mode constant ranges over [0.19600096779786974,1.2046269661757882], the inverse-spectrum trace over [0.44413751605172147,2.0052069566897663], and the finite quadratic harmonic envelope over [1.2140470537996502,7.467366756170776]. Every declared exponent in {1/2,2/3,3/4,4/5,9/10} passes the finite and infinite comparisons on all rows.
method: For every actual conditional likelihood row, form W=D_pi^(-1/2)L D_pi^(-1/2) and sort its d-1 positive eigenvalues.
For each declared alpha in (0,1), compute C_alpha=max_k k/lambda_k^alpha and assert the finite trace envelope.
Compare the finite zeta sum with the explicit integral tail for s=1/alpha>1.
Repeat the full volume-two cutoff, beta, source, history, order, prefix, adjoint and collar-orientation grid in independent code.
Use alpha=1, unsorted, exponent-inverted, linear-scaling, Fiedler-only and diagonal-generator mutations as hostile controls, then run the Lean scalar cross-check.
next_action: Prove one alpha in (0,1) and a positive uniform bound for its counting constant on one Hamiltonian common core; control it under cutoff, volume, source, phase and exhaustion changes; transfer the trace estimate to the R-399 conditional shell and combine it with the R-406 Schur residual split.
no_overclaim: The exponent family is a finite spectral inequality and a broader uniformity target; it is not an analytic regulator estimate, thermodynamic theorem, physical-sector result or QFT mass-gap proof.

qft_interface.closed: Finite spectral ordering, five declared sublinear envelopes, finite zeta-tail comparison, full likelihood-row coverage, hostile shortcut rejection and Lean scalar bookkeeping.
qft_interface.open: Uniform exponent and constant on a common Hamiltonian core, phase selection, shell transfer, common-alpha dynamics, broken-sector GNS coercivity, continuum and physical-gap obligations.

question: Can the normalized Green trace be controlled by some sublinear spectral-counting exponent rather than requiring the fixed quadratic envelope, and can one such exponent be made uniform on the physical route?
title: Sublinear spectral-counting exponent envelope for the normalized Green trace
